summary: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, causing every call to the external bank-partner-api to be rejected at the TLS handshake ('tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'). Onset is unambiguous: bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate from ~99% to ~2.5% starting in the 12:10–12:20 buckets, and a cert-watcher warned at 11:50. The HTTP error-rate dashboard stayed green because failed transfers are recorded asynchronously as PENDING_RETRY (ERROR logs) rather than as synchronous 5xx, so the 5xx-based panel sees nothing. No deployments occurred; the only config change (11:20 timeout bump) and flat request rate/p99 rule out deployment, config, capacity and partner-side-outage hypotheses. Root cause category: credential_expiry. Fix: renew/rotate the client certificate and restore bank calls; the PENDING_RETRY queue should be replayed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS client certificate breaks bank-partner-api calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. From that moment every call to the external bank-partner-api is rejected at the TLS handshake (alert 45), so fund transfers fail. Because failed transfers are recorded asynchronously as PENDING_RETRY rather than a synchronous 5xx, the HTTP error_rate panel stays green while bank_api_error_rate hits 100% and payment_success_rate drops to ~2.5%.

causal_chain.claim: Client cert reaches notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z without renewal (cert-watcher warned at 11:50)
Expiry -> mTLS handshake rejected with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'
Failed payments queued asynchronously as PENDING_RETRY (ERROR logs), so HTTP 5xx error_rate stays ~0.2%

assumptions: Certificate renewal is manual; no automated rotation occurred before expiry.
The 'expired certificate' remote error is caused by our own client cert (log explicitly names our CN and notAfter), not by a partner-side cert change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API outage / dependency failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank-partner-api is degraded or returning errors, causing transfers to fail (as in HIST-105).

causal_chain.claim: Partner API fails -> partner calls error -> payment failures

assumptions: Would require partner-side change, but no partner telemetry exists to confirm.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Error text names OUR client cert as expired (notAfter given), and a local cert-watcher warned 25 minutes before onset. The failure is at our TLS handshake (alert 45), not a partner 5xx; partner has no telemetry but the evidence points to our credential.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Timeout config change (bad deployment/config_change)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20 bank.api.timeout_ms change (3000->5000) caused the failures.
assumptions: A timeout increase could manifest as handshake cert errors (implausible).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Change landed 55 min before onset (11:20 vs 12:15) and the symptom is a TLS cert expiry matching notAfter exactly; p99 latency fell rather than rose, inconsistent with a timeout effect. No deployments occurred at all.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic surge / capacity saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A load spike saturated payment-service or its downstream and caused failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate was flat ~100 req/s and p99 latency decreased at onset; error is a deterministic TLS handshake rejection, not saturation.

facts.statement: payment-service logs show mTLS handshake failures naming our expired client cert: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'.
A cert-watcher warned at 11:50:26Z that the certificate would expire at 12:15:00Z.
bank_api_error_rate rose from ~0.2% to 100% starting in the 12:10–12:20 buckets.
payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~2.5% over the same buckets and remained there.
The HTTP 5xx error_rate metric stayed flat at ~0.2%, which is why the dashboard looked green.
Failed payments were recorded asynchronously as PENDING_RETRY errors (140 occurrences).
No code deployments occurred for any service in the incident window.
The only config change was bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z, 55 minutes before onset.
bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry; api-gateway and ledger-db logged no warnings/errors.
Request rate was flat (~100 req/s) and p99 latency fell at onset, ruling out load/saturation.
A past incident (HIST-106) had the identical 'client certificate expired; no renewal automation' signature.

assumptions: The 'expired certificate (alert 45)' remote error is triggered by our client certificate (the log names our CN and notAfter), not a partner-side certificate.
PENDING_RETRY payments are recoverable via retry/replay and were not permanently lost.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-2502: bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 (unrelated to onset)
cert-watcher warns client cert expires in 25 minutes (notAfter 12:15:00Z)
Client certificate expires; mTLS handshakes to bank-partner-api begin failing
First payment marked PENDING_RETRY due to rejected handshake
Support reports ~40 payment-failure tickets; HTTP error-rate panel still green

recommended_actions.action: Renew/rotate the payments-client client certificate for bank-partner-api and reload it in payment-service to restore mTLS handshakes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired cert (notAfter 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) is the direct cause of 100% bank API failures.

recommended_actions.action: Replay the queued PENDING_RETRY payments once connectivity is restored and reconcile against the bank.
recommended_actions.rationale: 140 payments were absorbed into a retry queue and may need explicit reprocessing.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alerting SLO on payment_success_rate and bank_api_error_rate (not just HTTP 5xx error_rate) so async-absorbed failures page on call.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 5xx error_rate panel stayed flat while ~97% of payments failed, hiding the incident.

recommended_actions.action: Implement automated certificate rotation with expiry alerting (as done after HIST-106) and make the cert-watcher warning actionable/paging.
recommended_actions.rationale: Same root cause recurred; renewal is manual and the 25-minute warning did not trigger action.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has no telemetry, so partner-side health cannot be independently confirmed; the conclusion rests on our own logs naming our expired client cert.

The first INFO-level payment-service log query (call tc-011) failed with invalid_arguments (missing start); a follow-up at 11:45-12:16 (tc-015, not truncated) showed no additional INFO events, but full INFO history was not exhaustively reviewed.
No data on when the certificate was last renewed or which secret store holds it, so the renewal-ownership gap is inferred from HIST-106 rather than observed.

findings.statement: bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 50% in the 12:10 bucket and 100% from the 12:20 bucket onward, remaining at 100% through 13:50.
payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.6% in the same 12:10/12:20 buckets and stayed near 2.5% (min 1.44) through 13:50, i.e. roughly 97% of payments failing.
The HTTP error_rate metric (5xx % of requests) stayed flat at ~0.2% across the whole window, never rising above max 0.32 — this is the green dashboard the report mentions.
140 ERROR logs show payments absorbed asynchronously: 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected', first seen 12:15:27Z.

refs.quote: payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected

findings.statement: No code deployments occurred for any service in 2026-04-02T11:00–13:59Z (count 0).
The only config change in the window was payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised from 3000 to 5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~55 minutes before onset.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with has_telemetry=false; there are no config changes recorded for it.
Payment request_rate stayed steady ~100 req/s before and during the incident (min 90.22, max 109.57), so the failure is not a traffic surge.
p99 latency dropped (320ms -> ~140ms) at onset rather than rising — consistent with requests failing fast at handshake instead of hanging.
No WARN/ERROR logs from api-gateway or ledger-db in the window, so upstream edge and shared database were not the source of the failure.

A prior incident HIST-106 (settlement-service, 2025-06-30) had the same signature: 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry, resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert'.

refs.quote: Client certificate expired; no renewal automation

findings.statement: Failures are logged at ERROR in payment-service but the synchronous HTTP path returns success (marked PENDING_RETRY, queued retry), so the 5xx-based error_rate panel cannot see them.
